deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page studies a discrete group E, the 'local' automorphisms of the free group pi = <l_0, l_1, l_inf | l_inf l_1 l_0 = 1>, the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,inf}. It is presented with generators rho, sigma_0, tau_0 as a quotient of (Z/2 x Z/2) * Z/3 by the relation [rho,sigma_0][rho^{-1},tau_0] = 1. E is an extension of Gamma = Gamma_{0,3}, the extended mapping class group of the 3-punctured sphere (about S_3 x Z/2: permutations of the punctures and orientation reversal), by the inner automorphisms of pi.

This page is a short programme note. One should still make explicit the extension S Gamma = S Gamma_{0,3} of Gamma by Z^{0,1,inf}. In modern terms S Gamma_{0,3} is the mapping class group of the pair of pants, the sphere with three boundary circles, allowing permutations of the boundaries and orientation reversal. Its kernel Z^3 is generated by the Dehn twists T_0, T_1, T_inf along the three boundary curves (equivalently the 'framings' or tangential data at the three points).

Then S E is defined as the fibre product S Gamma x_Gamma E. This gives a central-by-finite type enlargement of E: an extension of E by Z^3. It corresponds to keeping not only the conjugacy classes of the l_i but also the actual conjugating elements, i.e. tangential base points.

The next page carries this out in the profinite setting. It describes S E-hat-hat as tuples (p, sigma, g_0, g_1, g_inf) with p in Z-hat^*, sigma in S_3 and g_i in pi-hat, subject to a product relation. There is a map to Aut_loc(pi-hat) and an injection of pi-hat x Z-hat^{0,1,inf}; the factor Z-hat^3 acts by g_i -> g_i l_i^{alpha_i}, so it is exactly the profinite boundary-twist kernel. The purpose is the Teichmüller-tower / Galois-action programme: lift the action on the genus-0, 3-point piece to its 'bordered' (framed) version, so that pieces can be glued along boundaries.
errors: No mathematical claims are made, only a programme statement, so there is nothing to check. Note that the extension of S_3 x Z/2 by Z^3 is not obviously split. Orientation reversal acts on Z^3 by -1 and S_3 permutes the factors. A half-twist exchanging two boundary components squares to a product of boundary twists, cf. the ribbon/balancing identity c^2 = theta_{V⊗W}(theta_V^{-1} ⊗ theta_W^{-1}). So 'expliciter' is a genuine though elementary task.

ideas.what: Extension S Gamma_{0,3} of the extended mapping class group of the 3-punctured sphere by Z^3 (boundary Dehn twists), i.e. the mapping class group of the bordered pair of pants
ideas.modern_name: framed / bordered mapping class group of the pair of pants; boundary-twist central extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Dehn, Birman); used systematically in Teichmüller-tower work of Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmüller tower and surfaces with boundary/tangential data, but not this explicit extension

ideas.what: Defining S E = S Gamma x_Gamma E: a fibre product transporting boundary-twist data to the automorphism group of pi_1 of P^1 minus 3 points (profinitely: tuples with conjugators g_i, i.e. tangential base points)
ideas.modern_name: framed / tangential-base-point version of Aut_loc(pi_1), related to the ribbon (twist) extension in GT theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT, 1990) for the braided/ribbon version; Ihara and Nakamura for tangential base points and profinite descriptions

missed.claim: Grothendieck plans, but does not carry out on this page, an explicit description of the extension S Gamma_{0,3} and, by fibre product, of S E. The next page gives the profinite analogue via tuples (p, sigma, g_0, g_1, g_inf).
missed.quote: Il faudrait encore expliciter l'extension SΓ = SΓ_{0,3} de Γ par Z^{0,1,∞}, ce qui nous donnera (par produits fibrés) une description de SE = SΓ ×_Γ E.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early (1981) 'framed' version of the genus-0, 3-point building block of the Teichmüller tower, prefiguring the ribbon/twist extensions in later GT literature. The content is now standard, so it is mainly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: A three-line programme note announcing a routine computation: the boundary-twist extension of the pants mapping class group and its fibre product with the automorphism group. The ideas are standard and documented in later Teichmüller-tower and GT work; only the 1981 date is of mild historical interest.
